options.B: It stops ordinary citizens from asking questions
options.C: They are required by law to pay for all medical equipment
options.D: They must personally diagnose every sick patient

explanation: Local populations listen closely to their leaders, making their backing crucial for high community participation. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is true primary nursing often difficult to practice in busy public Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and high nurse-to-patient ratios make 24-hour individual accountability hard to maintain.
options.B: Patients in Nigeria prefer seeing a different nurse every hour for variety.
options.C: Physicians in Nigerian hospitals handle all bedside nursing duties themselves.
options.D: Nigerian nursing councils legally forbid registered nurses from writing patient care plans.

explanation: Real talk: managing a packed ward with limited hands means nurses often have to focus on quick tasks rather than continuous one-on-one primary care.

question: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 8 to 11 breaths per minute
options.B: 22 to 30 breaths per minute
options.C: 12 to 20 breaths per minute
options.D: 35 to 40 breaths per minute

explanation: A normal, healthy adult at rest breathes between 12 and 20 times every minute. Rates outside this range can indicate underlying respiratory or metabolic problems. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why do a pregnant woman's pelvic ligaments loosen up?

options.A: To prevent pressure on the urinary bladder
options.B: To compensate for weaker leg muscles
options.C: To allow increased movement for childbirth
options.D: To make sitting more comfortable

explanation: Nature is amazing! Hormones soften these ligaments during pregnancy so the pelvis can stretch and help the baby pass through easily.

question: Why do patients often feel so exhausted and confused right after a major fit?

options.A: The seizure permanently destroyed parts of their memory
options.B: Their blood pressure dropped to dangerous levels
options.C: Their brain cells used up a lot of energy and need to recover
options.D: They received too much medication during the episode

explanation: Think of a seizure like a sudden electrical storm in the brain. It burns through so much energy that the brain needs some quiet time to recharge afterwards. Completely normal recovery!

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

options.A: After the cleaning staff transport it outside
options.B: At the exact point and time of generation
options.C: Only when the waste bins are completely full
options.D: During the final incineration process

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately where the waste is produced to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which part of the penis directly wraps around and surrounds the urethra?

options.A: Dartos muscle layer
options.B: Corpus spongiosum
options.C: Corpora cavernosa
options.D: Tunica albuginea

explanation: Great job thinking through the anatomy! The corpus spongiosum is the single column of spongy tissue that houses and protects the urethra as it runs down to the tip.

question: What does 'accessibility' mean when we talk about community health services?

options.A: Services are restricted to wealthy individuals who can pay cash
options.B: Care reaches marginalized and remote populations without discrimination
options.C: Clinics remain closed on weekends to protect staff schedules
options.D: Patients must travel long distances to reach urban tertiary centers

explanation: Well done! Accessibility means making sure that healthcare breaks down barriers—whether financial or geographical—so that everyone who needs care can actually get it.

question: Why must patients with repaired heart defects take antibiotics before certain dental procedures?

options.A: To prevent infective endocarditis from bacteria entering the bloodstream
options.B: To lower their systemic blood pressure during the dental work
options.C: To keep their surgical chest incision from becoming dry
options.D: To prevent future heart rhythm changes after dental cleaning

explanation: Dental work can release bacteria into the blood. If it lands on repaired heart tissue, it can cause a serious infection called endocarditis. A dose of antibiotics keeps them safe!

question: At what age does a healthy baby usually double their birth weight?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At 12 months of age
options.C: At 2 months of age
options.D: At 5 months of age

explanation: Great job! A baby typically doubles their birth weight around 5 months and triples it by their first birthday.

question: Why is the sublingual route often chosen during a medical emergency?

options.A: It releases medicine slowly over twenty-four hours.
options.B: It prevents the patient from accidentally choking.
options.C: It allows the drug to enter the bloodstream very quickly.
options.D: It tastes much better than swallowed pills.

explanation: Rapid absorption bypasses digestion, providing fast symptom relief when every second counts. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h1)

question: What is the main goal of having both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems working together?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal body balance
options.B: Preventing the brain from ever sleeping
options.C: Keeping the heart rate as high as possible
options.D: Ensuring constant physical exhaustion

explanation: Both systems balance each other out to achieve homeostasis—a fancy word for keeping your internal body happy, stable, and healthy. Brilliant work!

question: Which of these examples shows a positive feedback mechanism in the body?

options.A: Thyroid hormone stopping TSH release from the anterior pituitary
options.B: Parathyroid hormone raising low blood calcium back to normal
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Insulin lowering blood glucose levels after a meal is eaten

explanation: Positive feedback pushes a process forward until a goal is reached! During childbirth, contractions release oxytocin, which causes even stronger contractions until the baby arrives.

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: Why were some people initially hesitant about modern family planning programs in Nigeria?

options.A: A total lack of trained nurses in every region of the country
options.B: Strict government bans on building hospitals and clinics
options.C: Cultural norms, religious beliefs, and mistrust of population policies
options.D: The complete absence of traditional birth spacing methods

explanation: Because these programs were newly introduced, many communities viewed them with suspicion, worrying about foreign population control motives.

question: Which of these is NOT an automatic (autonomic) body process linked to nerve degeneration?

options.A: Loss of normal bladder control
options.B: Sudden mastery of complex math skills
options.C: Drastic blood pressure drops when standing
options.D: Abnormal sweating patterns

explanation: You definitely don't gain superpowers from nerve degeneration! Autonomic functions control automatic things like blood pressure and sweating.

question: What should a nurse do if a low-risk pregnant woman develops severe anemia during her third trimester?

options.A: Advise her to drink more local herbal tea
options.B: Allow her to deliver at home with extra pillows
options.C: Disqualify her from home delivery and refer her to a hospital
options.D: Ignore the blood test results if she feels fine

explanation: Severe anemia puts the mother at high risk of postpartum hemorrhage, meaning she must deliver where blood transfusion is available. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the main goal when designing an operating room?

options.A: To protect patients from infection
options.B: To maximize hospital revenue
options.C: To store medical records safely
options.D: To provide space for family visits

explanation: Spot on! Everything in the operating room is carefully set up to keep germs away and stop surgical site infections before they start.

question: What is the primary goal of problem solving in nursing practice?

options.A: To delay vital patient care until doctors arrive
options.B: To reduce the number of shifts a nurse has to work
options.C: To replace the standard hospital administrative rules
options.D: To identify issues and ensure safe patient outcomes

explanation: Problem solving focuses on recognizing clinical issues quickly and taking action to keep patients safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a quiet sign that a nurse might be showing bias against a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing written educational pamphlets on nutrition
options.B: Unnecessarily delaying care or withholding proper pain relief
options.C: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes as ordered
options.D: Offering a clean hospital gown and warm blanket

explanation: Sometimes bias shows up as poor treatment—like making a patient wait too long or skipping proper pain meds because of personal judgment.

question: What is the primary function of the external female reproductive organs?

options.A: Protect internal organs from infection
options.B: Produce major female sex hormones
options.C: Produce mature eggs every month
options.D: Nourish a growing baby during pregnancy

explanation: The external genitalia act as a physical barrier to shield delicate internal reproductive tracts from pathogens and trauma. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: Who is responsible for making sure the nursing learning environment stays great?

options.A: Just the class reps in first year
options.B: Students, educators, and school administrators together
options.C: Exclusively the hospital medical director
options.D: Only the external licensing board

explanation: Building a wonderful nursing school environment takes teamwork. Everyone—from students to lecturers and management—has a role to play!

question: What is a major long-term risk of persistent, chronic inflammation in the body?

options.A: Rapid and permanent healing of all damaged joints
options.B: Progressive tissue destruction and organ dysfunction
options.C: Complete prevention of future bacterial infections
options.D: Immediate disappearance of all white blood cells

explanation: Chronic inflammation causes ongoing immune activity that slowly breaks down healthy tissue and impairs organ function. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the main underlying cause of uncontrolled cell growth in cancer?

options.A: Accumulated mutations in cellular DNA
options.B: Permanent resting state in the cells
options.C: A total lack of cellular respiration
options.D: Eating too many vitamins

explanation: You've got it! Cancer starts when genetic errors build up over time, breaking the normal rules that tell cells when to stop growing.

question: Why is an unconscious patient who is still breathing placed in the recovery position?

options.A: To make it easier to start an intravenous line
options.B: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway and allow drainage
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely
options.D: To prepare the patient for immediate surgery

explanation: You got it! This position keeps the airway safe by stopping the tongue from sliding back, and lets any saliva or vomit drain safely out of the mouth.

question: You are working with a nursing assistant on your team. Which of these tasks is safe and appropriate to delegate to them?

options.A: Assisting a stable patient with morning bath and hygiene
options.B: Assessing a newly admitted patient with chest pain
options.C: Administering intravenous medications to a critical patient
options.D: Changing the comprehensive nursing care plan

explanation: Correct! Nursing assistants are wonderful helpers trained for basic comfort measures like hygiene, while medications and assessments need your professional skills.

question: Which topical preparation is oil-based, greasy, and best suited for thick, dry, scaly skin lesions?

options.A: Aqueous solution
options.B: Gel
options.C: Ointment
options.D: Lotion

explanation: Ointments have a high oil content which creates a protective seal over the skin, locking in moisture and treating dry skin conditions effectively. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h3)

question: A nursing mum asks why her milk supply drops if she waits too long between feeds. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: Her breasts run out of physical space to store more fluid after a few hours
options.B: Infrequent suckling reduces prolactin surges and signals the body to slow production
options.C: The posterior pituitary gland stops working permanently after four hours of rest
options.D: Estrogen levels rise sharply every time the baby misses a scheduled feeding time

explanation: Spot on! Breastmilk works on a simple supply-and-demand rule. Less feeding means less hormone signaling, so the body makes less milk.

question: Which type of colostomy usually gives the most firm and solid stool?

options.A: Transverse colostomy
options.B: Sigmoid colostomy
options.C: Loop colostomy
options.D: Ascending colostomy

explanation: You got it! Because a sigmoid colostomy sits near the very end of the colon, the body has absorbed lots of water, leaving solid stool.

question: Which macronutrient requires the most energy for the body to digest and process?

options.A: Refined oil
options.B: Protein
options.C: Simple sugar
options.D: Dietary fat

explanation: Protein has a high thermic effect, forcing the body to expend more calories during its breakdown and metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h5)

question: How is formal nursing research different from just guessing or solving a ward problem on the spot?

options.A: Research follows a structured and disciplined pathway
options.B: Research never involves human participants
options.C: Research is always performed by doctors alone
options.D: Casual problem-solving uses more statistics

explanation: Spot on! While we solve ward problems every day, formal research follows careful, step-by-step rules to make sure the answers are truly reliable.

question: A patient asks for the best protein choice on a low-fat diet. What do you recommend?

options.A: Ribeye steak with visible marbling
options.B: Skinless chicken breast and white fish
options.C: Pork sausage links fried in oil
options.D: Deep-fried chicken wings with skin

explanation: Skinless poultry and white fish are naturally lean and low in fat compared to red meats or fried options.

question: A glass bottle of lab specimen drops and shatters on the floor, creating a large spill. What should you do first?

options.A: Cover the glass shards with a cloth sheet
options.B: Leave the room and wait for the housekeeping staff to notice
options.C: Put on appropriate PPE and obtain a designated spill kit
options.D: Mop the floor quickly with a dry paper towel

explanation: Spot on! Safety first: always wear your PPE before dealing with broken glass and body fluids to protect yourself from exposure.

question: What does active immunization (like a vaccine) trigger the body to make?

options.A: Temporary foreign plasma proteins
options.B: Non-specific physical skin barriers
options.C: Immediate exogenous red blood cells
options.D: Its own antibodies and memory cells

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines train your body to do the heavy lifting by creating its own long-lasting antibodies and memory cells.

question: You need cheap gloves for quick, low-risk tasks where tearing isn't a big worry. Which material is best?

options.A: Latex
options.B: Vinyl
options.C: Surgical
options.D: Nitrile

explanation: Vinyl is budget-friendly and latex-free, making it ideal for quick, low-risk chores where you don't need heavy-duty strength.

question: What is the ultimate aim of a community health nurse in mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity so the community runs its own health programs
options.B: Collecting data to publish research papers in medical journals
options.C: Making sure the local clinic receives a large budget from abroad
options.D: Ensuring the nurse becomes the most respected person in the village

explanation: The goal of community mobilisation is self-reliance, where locals have the skills to manage their health without constant outside intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why might a patient with low oxygen levels first appear restless and confused?

options.A: Restlessness is a side effect of normal breathing
options.B: The patient's stomach is empty during the assessment
options.C: The patient is reacting to cold hospital room temperatures
options.D: The brain is sensitive to a shortage of oxygen

explanation: Brain tissue needs a constant, heavy supply of oxygen, so even mild shortages quickly cause mental changes like confusion or anxiety. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is food safety such a big priority for community health nurses?

options.A: It directly reduces preventable gastrointestinal infections
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for community health clinics
options.C: It is the only way to treat chronic medical conditions
options.D: It stops all forms of malnutrition instantly

explanation: Spot on! When we teach and practice good food safety, we cut down massively on those painful, preventable stomach infections that bring patients into our clinics.

question: Why do patients with advanced occupational lung diseases have an increased risk of heart failure?

options.A: Respiratory failure lowers the body temperature until the heart stops beating
options.B: The inhaled mineral dust travels directly into the heart muscle and clogs valves
options.C: Scarred lung tissue restricts blood flow, forcing the right heart to pump much harder
options.D: Lung damage causes the patient to drink excessive amounts of salty water

explanation: Destruction of the pulmonary capillary bed increases vascular resistance, putting immense strain on the right side of the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: What kind of pain do adjuvant medications like gabapentin usually target?

options.A: Sudden high fever from bacterial infection
options.B: Acute inflammatory joint swelling
options.C: Neuropathic pain from damaged nerves
options.D: Severe stomach cramping from food poisoning

explanation: Gabapentin and similar drugs are originally seizure medicines, but they work wonders for that burning, shooting pain caused by damaged nerves.

question: Why should nurses avoid relying solely on a patient's verbal report about taking their medications?

options.A: Patients often claim they take pills even when they miss them
options.B: Patients never remember the names of their prescribed drugs
options.C: Verbal reports are illegal to record in hospital charts
options.D: Doctors prefer laboratory tests over talking to patients

explanation: Patients want to please their healthcare providers and often say they take their medications faithfully when they actually do not. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a great example of the 'Right Assessment' in action?

options.A: Checking blood pressure before giving an antihypertensive drug
options.B: Asking the patient what their favorite food is for breakfast
options.C: Cleaning the bedside table before placing a water cup
options.D: Reading the hospital policy manual on intravenous access

explanation: Right assessment means checking vital signs or lab results first to make sure the drug is actually safe to give right now.

question: Why is an obstetric ultrasound often performed when evaluating a patient with severe hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To check for multiple gestation or molar pregnancy
options.B: To see if the liver is enlarged from fluid backup
options.C: To measure the exact thickness of the stomach lining
options.D: To test the baby's hearing and nervous system

explanation: Conditions like twins or a molar pregnancy cause much higher levels of hormones, which can trigger worse vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h3)

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease shows signs of metabolic acidosis. What lab result would a nurse expect to see?

options.A: An elevated blood pH well above 7.45
options.B: An increased respiratory rate causing carbon dioxide retention
options.C: A high concentration of bicarbonate in the fresh urine
options.D: A low serum bicarbonate level on the lab report

explanation: Spot on! Metabolic acidosis means the body is low on its main buffer, so you'll see a drop in serum bicarbonate levels on the patient's lab results.

question: What causes the blood vessels in a newborn's lungs to relax and open up at birth?

options.A: Expansion of the lungs with air and a rise in oxygen
options.B: An increase in pressure from the clamped umbilical cord
options.C: The sudden drop in body temperature outside the womb
options.D: The release of digestive enzymes into the bloodstream

explanation: When the baby takes that magical first breath, the rush of oxygen tells the lung blood vessels to relax and open wide for business! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: What is a major challenge in providing adolescent reproductive care in many communities?

options.A: The requirement that all nurses undergo legal training before practice
options.B: A complete lack of teenage patients visiting urban health facilities
options.C: Conflict between traditional moral disapproval and young people's health needs
options.D: An absolute nationwide ban on importing any modern contraceptive items

explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs often clash with the clinical reality that teens need reproductive health support. Navigating this is part of nursing!

question: Which activity is a key community prevention strategy for GBV in displacement settings?

options.A: Establishing safe spaces for women and girls
options.B: Banning all public gatherings and educational meetings
options.C: Locking all community members inside their tents at night
options.D: Stopping all clinical treatment services in displacement camps

explanation: Safe spaces give women and girls a secure area to gather, find peer support, and join community empowerment programs.

question: What is the very first thing you should do for someone with a minor burn?

options.A: Cool the burn with running tap water for ten to twenty minutes
options.B: Pop any small blisters immediately to release trapped fluid
options.C: Place crushed ice directly onto the raw wound area
options.D: Apply thick butter or cooking oil to seal the exposed skin

explanation: Correct! Cool running water takes the heat out of the skin fast, stops the burn from going deeper, and eases the pain safely.

question: What is the medical term for a deep bone infection that can happen if a bite goes all the way down to the bone?

options.A: Cellulitis
options.B: Tenosynovitis
options.C: Fasciitis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteomyelitis means an infection has reached the bone and bone marrow. It's a serious complication we try to prevent with prompt wound care and antibiotics.

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.A: The government pays monthly stipends for large households
options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

explanation: Spot on! In farming communities, children help out on the farm and support their parents as they grow older.

question: A community health nurse notices a sudden rush of parents requesting routine check-ups for young girls right before long school holidays. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Families preparing daughters for upcoming FGM ceremonies
options.B: Standard preventive screening recommended by public health
options.C: A sudden regional outbreak of adolescent infections
options.D: Parents seeking routine sports physicals for school teams

explanation: School holidays are prime time when families travel home or arrange for girls to undergo FGM. Always stay alert for these patterns in community practice!

question: What is the primary trigger for hypovolemic shock?

options.A: An infection spreading through the bloodstream
options.B: A rapid drop in circulating blood volume
options.C: An acute blockage in the coronary arteries
options.D: A sudden spike in blood pressure

explanation: Hypovolemic shock happens when the body loses a massive amount of fluid or blood, leaving the circulatory system with too little volume to fill the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: What is polypharmacy?

options.A: The practice of buying fake drugs from unlicensed local market vendors
options.B: The manufacturing of herbal remedies without standard quality control
options.C: The storage of expired pharmaceutical products in hospital pharmacy stores
options.D: The simultaneous use of multiple medications by a single patient

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to a patient taking multiple medications concurrently, which raises the risk of drug interactions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Health Services?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on the treatment of geriatric illnesses
options.B: Banning teenagers from visiting local community pharmacies
options.C: Providing confidential and accessible care without judgment
options.D: Requiring parental consent for every routine consultation

explanation: That's right! Youth-friendly centers remove barriers like judgmental attitudes and lack of privacy so young people feel safe seeking help.

question: How often should vital signs be monitored immediately after an MVA procedure during the first hour?

options.A: Only if the patient complains of dizziness
options.B: Every hour on the hour
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Frequent checks every 15 minutes during the first hour help catch early signs of hemorrhage or vasovagal shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: What is the main goal of giving lots of intravenous (IV) fluids during a pain crisis?

options.A: To lower the patient's body temperature and stop low-grade fevers
options.B: To dilute circulating bilirubin and immediately clear skin jaundice
options.C: To stimulate the bone marrow to produce healthy round red blood cells
options.D: To reduce blood viscosity and help clear microvascular blockages

explanation: Fluids are great medicine here! Giving IV fluids thins out the blood (reduces viscosity), helping it flow more easily past those tiny blockages caused by sickled cells.

question: Why do nurses pre-test IEC support materials before mass production?

options.A: To check if the target audience understands and accepts the message
options.B: To prove to the hospital management that the nurse can draw well
options.C: To increase the market price of the printed paper leaflets
options.D: To test if the printer ink can resist heavy rainfall

explanation: Pre-testing saves time and money by making sure people actually understand the pictures and text before you print thousands of copies.

question: Why does a peri-operative nurse need both strong clinical skills and great communication?

options.A: Operating rooms prohibit verbal communication during procedures.
options.B: The nursing council mandates dual certification for all surgical staff.
options.C: Patients face high physical risks and emotional stress during surgery.
options.D: Surgeons require nurses to manage hospital administrative duties.

explanation: Surgery is a big deal! Patients and their families go through a lot of physical and emotional stress, so nurses need to be skilled and comforting.

question: Why do people with untreated mental health challenges sometimes run a higher risk of substance abuse?

options.A: Their bodies process alcohol much faster than healthy people do
options.B: Mental illness completely stops the brain from feeling physical pain
options.C: They may use drugs to self-medicate and escape emotional pain
options.D: Prescription drugs for mental illness always cause chemical addiction

explanation: Spot on. When professional mental health support isn't available, some people unfortunately turn to substances just to numb heavy feelings like anxiety or depression.

question: Why are babies and young children extra vulnerable to the risks of self-medication?

options.A: They refuse to swallow any medication unless it is sweet
options.B: Their liver and kidney enzyme systems are still immature
options.C: Their skin absorbs chemical substances much slower than adults
options.D: They have higher blood volume than healthy adults

explanation: Spot on! Children's bodies process drugs differently because their organs aren't fully developed yet to clear toxins easily.

question: Which of these is a great example of a well-written community health goal?

options.A: To teach nurses how to write better charts during night shifts
options.B: To reduce childhood malnutrition in Ward 4 by 20% within six months
options.C: To talk about malaria prevention whenever people visit the clinic
options.D: To make sure everybody in the whole country feels much healthier this year

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, tells you where it's happening, gives a clear percentage, and sets a realistic timeframe.

question: Why might an elderly patient talk about tummy aches and poor appetite instead of crying when they are grieving?

options.A: Older adults often express emotional pain through physical body complaints
options.B: Physical pain always replaces sadness in older people
options.C: Grief only affects the tummy and never the brain
options.D: They are just trying to get extra attention from the nurses

explanation: Spot on! Older adults often show emotional hurt through physical signs, known as somatic symptoms. Always keep an eye out for this in clinical practice.

question: Why does the inner lining of the small intestine contain millions of villi and microvilli?

options.A: To secrete large amounts of digestive enzymes straight into the mouth
options.B: To maximize the surface area available for absorbing nutrients
options.C: To produce strong muscular contractions for moving food forward
options.D: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming directly from the stomach

explanation: The villi and microvilli create a massive surface area that allows digested food particles to pass efficiently into the blood and lymph vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is a key piece of advice to give a patient who just received praziquantel treatment?

options.A: You must complete a strict 14-day course of tablets to ensure the larvae in your skin die.
options.B: The drug kills adult worms, but you can still get infected again if you swim in contaminated streams.
options.C: You should take the pills on an empty stomach to prevent the drug from dissolving too quickly.
options.D: The medication will immediately reverse any scar tissue already formed in your bladder.

explanation: Praziquantel wipes out the worms currently inside, but it doesn't give you superpowers against future infections. Patient education is our superpower as nurses!

question: Why do nurses need to master drug dosage calculations?

options.A: To prevent medication errors and keep patients safe
options.B: To save money on pharmacy supplies
options.C: To speed up morning rounds
options.D: To skip calling the doctor

explanation: Calculations act as your final safety net to make sure patients get the exact right dose—no more, no less. You've got this!

question: Where does a standard public health agency mainly get its money to run?

options.A: The national government budget
options.B: Direct patient consultation fees
options.C: Commercial bank loans
options.D: Private corporate investors

explanation: You've got this! Public agencies are run directly by the government, so they rely mostly on funds from the national treasury to keep things moving.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to accurately track fluid balance for a pregnant patient with acute kidney injury?

options.A: Using an indwelling urinary catheter for strict hourly output measurement
options.B: Asking the patient to estimate how many times she urinates each day
options.C: Weighing the patient once every morning after breakfast
options.D: Checking skin turgor and mucous membrane moisture every shift

explanation: When kidneys are in trouble, hourly checks via catheter give us the exact numbers we need to see if treatments are working.

question: What is a key nursing strategy for helping patients prevent complications from chronic skin conditions?

options.A: Teaching the patient how to recognize early flare-ups and avoid known triggers
options.B: Stopping all topical medications as soon as the skin looks slightly better
options.C: Using harsh antiseptic scrubs every day to remove the outer skin layer
options.D: Encouraging the patient to isolate themselves from family and friends

explanation: You got it! Empowering patients to spot early warning signs and steer clear of their triggers stops small issues from blowing up into major infections.

question: Which of these is a very common reason to perform a laparoscopy?

options.A: Extraction of kidney stones
options.B: Drainage of a cerebral abscess
options.C: Repair of a fractured femur bone
options.D: Removal of an inflamed appendix

explanation: Brilliant! Removing an appendix using tiny cuts (laparoscopic appendectomy) is a very common and safe way to treat appendicitis.

question: When would you choose a simple straight catheter instead of a permanent Foley catheter?

options.A: When the patient is unconscious in the intensive care unit
options.B: When a patient needs periodic bladder emptying without a permanent bag
options.C: When the patient has a severe urethral blockage
options.D: When long-term continuous monitoring of hourly urine output is required

explanation: You nailed it! Straight catheters are popped in to drain the bladder and taken right back out, which lowers the risk of infection compared to leaving a tube in all day.

question: Which physical assessment finding is most characteristic of chronic motor nerve damage in the lower extremities?

options.A: Uncontrollable muscle expansion
options.B: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Muscle atrophy and foot drop
options.D: Sudden involuntary limb sweating

explanation: When motor nerves stop stimulating leg muscles, the muscles shrink (atrophy), and the muscles lifting the front of the foot become too weak, leading to foot drop. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h4)

question: Why do nurses set specific alert limits (thresholds) on patient wearables?

options.A: To ensure the device battery never runs out of power unexpectedly
options.B: To stop patients from looking at their own heart rate data
options.C: To comply with government laws regarding smartphone manufacturing
options.D: To prevent alert fatigue from minor, harmless data fluctuations

explanation: Setting smart limits stops alarms from ringing over tiny movements, keeping nurses focused on actual emergencies.

question: Why do international agreements like the Cairo Programme of Action matter for local Nigerian nursing practice?

options.A: They allow nurses to bypass local hospital rules during emergency obstetric procedures
options.B: They eliminate the need for patient consent in family planning clinics
options.C: They legally require international organizations to fund all local nursing salaries
options.D: They provide a standard framework that governments use to shape national health policies and clinic guidelines

explanation: Big global agreements help shape our national laws and clinic guidelines, which directly guide the safe and effective care you will provide to your patients.

question: Which heart chamber pumps oxygen-rich blood out into the main body artery (the aorta)?

options.A: Left ventricle
options.B: Right atrium
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle is the powerhouse of the heart! It has the thickest walls because it has to push blood all the way around the entire body.

question: What is the biggest challenge faced by child-headed households?

options.A: The government evicts them immediately for breaking zoning laws
options.B: Children lack adult guidance, financial stability, and legal protection
options.C: They are required by law to run community health clinics
options.D: They receive too much financial support from international donors

explanation: When young ones live alone without an adult, everyday survival becomes a massive struggle for food, shelter, and safety. Community nurses play a key role in identifying and helping them.

question: Which model explains that people change their habits by moving through steps like thinking about it, and then finally taking action?

options.A: The Biomedical Treatment Model
options.B: The Environmental Sanitation Grid
options.C: The Germ Theory of Disease
options.D: The Transtheoretical Model

explanation: Well done! The Transtheoretical Model breaks down the journey of change from early thoughts all the way to long-term maintenance.

question: A patient is due for digoxin, but their pulse is 52 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Crush the tablet to speed up its absorption in the stomach
options.B: Hold the medication and notify the prescribing physician
options.C: Give half the dose now and the other half later in the day
options.D: Administer the medication with a glass of orange juice

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Digoxin slows the heart down, so a pulse below 60 means it's safer to hold the drug and call the doctor.

question: Why should we involve parents and community leaders in adolescent health programs?

options.A: To shift cultural norms and build supportive safety nets for teens
options.B: To give adults total control over adolescent personal decisions
options.C: To ensure healthcare facilities collect more financial profit
options.D: To eliminate the need for professional nursing staff

explanation: Correct! When community leaders and parents are on board, stigma drops and teenagers find a safer network to ask for help.

question: What is an example of secondary epidemiologic data?

options.A: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of children
options.B: Interviewing village elders about local health beliefs
options.C: Conducting blood pressure checks at a local market square
options.D: Reviewing past mortality records from the health ministry

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that was already gathered by other agencies or researchers in the past. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the most common first imaging test used to check for uterine fibroids?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Abdominal X-ray
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Electrocardiogram

explanation: A pelvic ultrasound is safe, quick, and gives a clear picture of the uterus without exposing the patient to radiation.

question: What is the main purpose of a draw sheet placed across the middle of a hospital bed?

options.A: To replace the need for a standard bottom sheet
options.B: To help lift, turn, and reposition the patient easily
options.C: To serve as an extra blanket during cold night shifts
options.D: To catch food crumbs during meal delivery times

explanation: Correct! A draw sheet acts like a handy helper, letting you slide or turn a patient smoothly without causing friction burns or shear injuries.

question: What is the primary job of the respiratory center in the medulla?

options.A: Filtering dust and germs out of inhaled air
options.B: Setting the basic rhythm and depth of breathing
options.C: Exchanging oxygen across the lung membranes
options.D: Producing mucus to keep the airway moist

explanation: The medullary respiratory center automatically drives the inhale-and-exhale cycle without needing conscious thought. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to swallow strong painkillers to hide tummy ache?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent blindness in all affected adults
options.B: It permanently lowers a patient's normal body temperature
options.C: It can delay the diagnosis of a serious condition like appendicitis
options.D: It automatically cures any underlying infection within a few hours

explanation: Pain is your body's warning alarm! Masking it with painkillers might trick you into thinking you're fine while a serious emergency like appendicitis gets worse.

question: A scared patient asks if the metal pins will hurt going into their head. What should you say?

options.A: You will feel a sharp pain, but it will go away as soon as the weights are hung.
options.B: Do not worry, the pins are very small and just rest on top of your hair.
options.C: Most patients are asleep during the whole process so they never feel anything.
options.D: The doctor will numb your scalp with medicine first so you won't feel sharp pain.

explanation: Always be honest and comforting! Letting them know the doctor will numb the area first builds great trust and calms their nerves.

question: What is the main job of the fallopian tubes in the female body?

options.A: To serve as the usual site for fertilization of the egg
options.B: To provide a muscular environment for fetal development
options.C: To secrete large amounts of protective progesterone
options.D: To produce the monthly supply of mature oocytes

explanation: You nailed it! The fallopian tubes catch the released egg and act as the meeting place where sperm usually fertilize it before it moves to the uterus.

question: How are the tiny bony struts inside cancellous bone arranged?

options.A: In a random web with no fixed pattern
options.B: In circular rings around a central canal
options.C: Along lines of physical stress
options.D: In thick parallel sheets along the bone shaft

explanation: Think of how a bridge is built to handle heavy loads! These tiny struts (called trabeculae) arrange themselves dynamically right along the lines where the bone feels the most physical stress and pressure from daily movement.

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have.

question: How does water mostly travel across the lining of the large intestine?

options.A: Pumping uphill against concentration gradients
options.B: Evaporating through the abdominal wall
options.C: Following active sodium transport passively
options.D: Being pushed by direct muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow salt! As the gut actively pumps sodium across its lining, water follows it smoothly through osmosis.

question: What is the main goal of cancer rehabilitation?

options.A: Curing the primary cancer diagnosis
options.B: Preventing the recurrence of tumors
options.C: Managing acute surgical site infections
options.D: Restoring physical and emotional well-being

explanation: You got this! Cancer rehab is all about helping patients get back their strength, independence, and good quality of life after treatment.

question: Why do doctors sometimes order a contrast angiogram for someone with severe peripheral vascular disease?

options.A: To map out the exact spot and size of blocked arteries
options.B: To measure electrical signals in the leg muscles
options.C: To see if the patient has high blood pressure overall
options.D: To check how long it takes for a blood sample to clot

explanation: An angiogram uses a special dye to take clear pictures of the blood vessels, acting like a roadmap so doctors can see exactly where the blockages are.
